chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The worst of people in the presence of Allah on the Day of Judgment are those who are honored out of fear of their evil.'

key_terms.اتِّقَاءَ شَرِّهِمْ: Out of fear of their evil

ai.seo_question: Who are the worst people in the sight of Allah on the Day of Judgment according to this hadith?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this hadith from *Al-Kafi* critiques the social phenomenon of *ittiqāʾ al-sharr* (fearing one's evil), where respect is granted based on power or potential harm rather than moral merit. It serves as a warning against superficial honor and highlights the divine preference for those whose status is rooted in genuine virtue rather than the fear of their capacity to cause damage.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘The most evil of the people in the Presence of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> on the Day of Judgment will be those who were honoured (in the world) out of fear of their evil’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from al-Nawfali from al-Sakuni from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following:
“The Messenger of Allah has said, ‘The most evil among people in the sight of Allah on the Day of Judgment will be the one whom people respect for fear from his evil manners.’”
